findings.title: _bs_iv_vectorized Newton diverges for OTM calls and returns non-converged values as valid IVs (shared by the Greeks surface, NN labels and NN benchmark)
findings.description: The starting value is the Brenner-Subrahmanyam guess sqrt(2*pi/T)*C/F, clipped to at least 0.05. For OTM calls, C is small, so the start is 0.05, which sits in the flat convex region where vega is about 0. The first Newton step jumps to the 5.0 clip, and after that the iterate bounces between 1e-4 and 5.0. The loop has no bracket and no damping. It never marks a non-converged entry as NaN: it returns whatever the last iterate was, usually 1e-4. Callers drop these with ad-hoc filters (iv>=0.005 in risk_monitor, iv>=0.02 in NN data and benchmark), so the failures vanish silently instead of being reported. The docstring's claim that Newton is 'guaranteed to converge ... because BS is convex and monotone in sigma' is false. The Black-Scholes price is convex in sigma only below the inflection point sigma*=sqrt(2|ln F/K|/T). Starting from the inflection point is the Manaster-Koehler (1982) start, which guarantees monotone convergence. Consequences: see nngreeks-greeks-surface-published-wrong, nngreeks-nn-benchmark-unrepresentative and nngreeks-nn-training-domain.
findings.evidence: Round trip on 200,000 exact Black-Scholes prices over the NN training domain (x=ln K/F in U[-0.30,0.25], T in U[0.02,2], sigma in U[0.08,0.6], well-posed OTM price >1e-8 F): shipped solver gets 8.20% wrong by more than 1e-6. By moneyness: 28.5% fail for x in [0.10,0.25) and 3.7% for [0.05,0.10). When the guess is clipped at 0.05, 69.3% fail. Failures return <=1e-3. Heston examples (baseline params, T=0.25): x=0.117 price $16.26 gives 1.00e-04 (reference 0.1572); x=0.091 price $48.11 gives 1.00e-04 (reference 0.1773). On the 500-option benchmark set the loop always runs the full max_iter=50 iterations. Reference: independent Lewis/Carr-Madan quad pricer plus brentq (scratchpad work/ref2.py). The existing test test_roundtrip_skew_range still passes with 3 of 100 wrong (true 0.133 returned as 0.0001) because it tolerates 5% errors, and its 'valid.sum()>=80' check is vacuous since the solver never returns NaN.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Change the start to the Manaster-Koehler inflection point: sigma0 = sqrt(2*|ln(F/K)|/T), clipped to [0.05, 3]. On the same 200k set this alone gives 0.000% wrong (max err under 1e-10) at the same speed, and 16 iterations instead of 50 on the benchmark set. (2) After the loop, NaN out entries that did not converge (|last step| > tol), so failures are no longer returned as values. (3) Better still, invert the OTM price (put via parity when K<F) inside a maintained [lo,hi] bisection bracket (safeguarded Newton, prototype in scratchpad work/iv_fix.py: 0 failures, max err 9e-11), or use Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational'. (4) Move the solver out of nn_pricer into a torch-free module (see nngreeks-torch-coupling). Tests: exact-BS round trip over a dense (x,T,sigma) grid asserting max err <1e-8 and no NaN for well-posed prices. Also compare against brentq on 1,000 Heston prices, asserting NaN only where the OTM price is below the pricer noise floor.

findings.title: Published Greeks surface: 21/90 grid nodes silently dropped (13 well-posed, prices $0.01-$153), 8 of the 69 shown nodes carry IVs fabricated from pricer noise; unstable nodes, max vomma and mean-vanna signs are artifacts
findings.description: The '69-cell/69-node grid' (README, substack, page badge) is not a design choice. The grid is 6 maturities x 15 strikes = 90 nodes, and 69 is the number of nodes where the broken solver happened to converge. Almost the whole OTM-call wing is missing. Separately, heston_call_batch has an absolute price error of about 3e-4 index points (batch minus reference is about +3.3e-4 on far-OTM strikes). Inverting prices below that floor fabricates IVs: the 14d smile rises to 28.7% at x=+0.25, where the true Heston price is about 1e-14, and the 30d smile dips to 5.0% and then climbs back to 20%. The same parquet feeds the calibration page's 'SPX Implied Volatility Smile - All Maturities', so these fake wings are live on navnoorbawa.me/calibration.html. They are visible in the page's matSmiles JSON: 14d iv [...,22.379,12.105,16.357,20.773,24.906,28.746]; 30d [...,22.401,4.999,10.251,20.155]. Every downstream statistic on the Greeks page changes once the surface is computed correctly.
findings.evidence: Reproduced the parquet bit-for-bit (max |iv diff| 3.3e-13) with kappa=4.62, theta=0.0764, sigma=0.84, rho=-0.99, v0=0.0561, S=6581, r=.045, q=.013. Compared each node with a high-precision Carr-Madan quad reference at the same params. DROPPED with well-posed prices include 365d x=+0.171 ($152.7, ref IV 0.1997), 180d x=+0.132 ($63.8, 0.1769), 91d x=+0.093 ($40.3, 0.1697), 14d x=+0.054 ($6.58, 0.1794). WRONG: 14d x=+0.093..+0.25 published 0.121/0.164/0.208/0.249/0.287 where the reference price is 9e-7..0; 30d x=+0.132/+0.211/+0.25 published 0.050/0.1025/0.2016 where the price is about 1e-12..0. Rebuilt with a bracketed OTM solver plus a price floor of OTM price >1e-5 F: 71 nodes; max vomma 12,246 (published 4,086); mean vomma 2,263 (published 1,268). Unstable nodes change completely: (180d,+0.171), (365d,+0.211), (365d,+0.25) instead of the published (365d,-0.30), (365d,-0.26), (365d,+0.13). Mean vanna by maturity changes sign at the long end: 180d -0.144 becomes +0.126, 365d -0.005 becomes +0.284. The applied fix alone (Manaster-Koehler start, no floor) gives 89 nodes but keeps the fabricated 30d wing (0.136, 0.171, 0.202 at x>=0.171), so the floor is required. The report_generator text 'Three nodes ... 1Y deep OTM puts (log_m = -0.30, -0.26) and 1Y far OTM call (+0.13)' and backtest_engine 'C6: 3 unstable vomma nodes' are hard-coded from the broken surface.
findings.proposed_fix: In compute_greeks_surface: use the fixed solver, invert the OTM price (put via parity for K<F), and keep a node only if its OTM forward price is above a floor tied to pricer accuracy (e.g. >1e-5*F, or at least 100x the measured |batch-quad| error). Log the number of dropped nodes and why they were dropped, and fail loudly if more than about 10% are dropped. Regenerate the parquet (see nngreeks-greeks-surface-frozen-provenance for which params). Replace the hard-coded counts and node descriptions in README, substack, greeks.html, report_generator and backtest_engine with values derived from the data. Test: build the default surface for a fixed param set and assert every node's IV is within 1e-4 of an independent quad+brentq reference, and that no node with reference price >$0.05 is missing.

findings.title: Greeks Risk Monitor is a 6-month-old one-off: built with rho=-0.99 (outside HESTON_BOUNDS), never regenerated, no provenance, and plotted next to unrelated live parameters
findings.description: Nothing in the repo calls RiskMonitor or compute_greeks_surface except the tests: not cloud_refresh, not the daily workflow, no script. The shipped parquet was produced by hand from the rounded docstring params (rho=-0.99, sigma=0.84). That rho is outside the current HESTON_BOUNDS rho floor of -0.95, and it differs from both baseline_2026-03-24.json (rho=-0.95) and every archived calibration. The page describes a spot of 6,581; the DB's last SPX close is 7,500.58 (2026-06-18), and the live site's calibration is from 2026-09-11. The parquet stores no params, S, r, q or source calibration, so provenance can only be recovered by reverse engineering. Its as_of_date is '2026-03-25', because RiskMonitor defaults as_of_date to date.today(), which is the run date rather than the market date. The page badge hard-codes '2026-03-24'. The calibration page draws its 'SPX Implied Volatility Smile - All Maturities' from this parquet beside a 'Calibrated Parameter Summary' of the live fit. The live page shows kappa=5.00, theta=0.0431, sigma=0.657, rho=-0.95, sqrt(v0)=10.43%, but the smile's ATM IVs are about 22-25%, generated from sqrt(v0)=23.7%. Nothing tells the reader that the two panels describe different models, and no staleness warning appears anywhere.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'RiskMonitor|compute_greeks_surface|risk_monitor' over scripts/, .github/, dashboard/ and joint_vol_calibration/ (excluding tests) finds only the definition and delta_hedger's import of _bs_vomma. Exact reproduction of the parquet with rho=-0.99 (max |iv| diff 3.3e-13). With the baseline rho=-0.95 the result is 68 nodes and different values. Live calibration.html (fetched 2026-09-24) shows 'Correlation rho -0.95 ... Spot vol sqrt(v0) 10.43%' in the same grid row as the smile chart, whose data starts {'T':14,'iv':[38.916,...]}. Parquet: as_of_date unique ['2026-03-25']. greeks.html:9 has the literal '2026-03-24'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Greeks step to scripts/cloud_refresh.py. After a calibration is accepted (latest_good_calibration_path), build RiskMonitor(S=session spot, r=session ^IRX, q=the q the calibrator used, params=that calibration, as_of_date=its market date) and save it. Persist provenance columns or parquet metadata: params, S, r, q, calibration filename, code version. In load_page2/load_page3, read as_of_date and params from the parquet, show them in the badge, and add a staleness banner when they differ from the displayed calibration or are more than N sessions old. Build the calibration-page smile from the displayed params, or label it as a different model. Test: a dashboard test asserting the greeks badge date equals the parquet as_of_date, and that the smile's params match load_page2's displayed params.

findings.title: NN claims cannot be reproduced from a clean clone: train_network crashes on current torch; weights gitignored; initialisation unseeded; training path untested (24 tests always skip in CI)
findings.description: ReduceLROnPlateau(..., verbose=False) raises TypeError on torch >= 2.6, where the 'verbose' kwarg was removed. requirements.txt pins only torch>=2.0.0, and CI installs the latest CPU wheel, so every fresh environment crashes. That covers train_spx, train_vix and NNPricer.load(), which auto-trains by default. The .pt weights and mc_cache are gitignored, so the 18 weight-dependent and 6 cache-dependent tests always skip in CI, and nothing in the suite exercises train_network. The failure has therefore never surfaced. torch.manual_seed(RANDOM_SEED) runs after HestonNet(...) is constructed, so weight initialisation is unseeded and two identical runs give different models. The README/substack figures '8.1x speedup, MAE < 0.07 (0.068) vol pts' cannot be regenerated or verified. The weights are small (the SPX checkpoint is 0.80 MB), so the gitignore comment 'Large ML training data' does not apply to them.
findings.evidence: Clean-clone reproduction in a private copy: generate_spx_training_data() ran for 468 s (500,000 rows, 425,307 after the IV filter), then train_spx() failed with 'TypeError: ReduceLROnPlateau.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument verbose' (torch 2.14.0+cpu; inspect.signature shows no verbose parameter). With a shim that drops the kwarg, two identical single-thread runs of train_network on the same 20k rows gave val_mse 1.539e-4 and 8.413e-5. A checkpoint saved from that run is 802,517 bytes. A full-size retrain under shared-CPU load reached only epoch 20 (val_rmse 0.51 vp) after about 29 min, so the 0.068 vp claim was not reproducible within the audit window.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove verbose=False (or build the kwargs from the scheduler's signature). Call torch.manual_seed before constructing the model and also seed numpy. Pin a tested torch range (e.g. torch>=2.2,<3). Add a fast test that trains on about 5k rows for 2 epochs into tmp_path and checks that the checkpoint round-trips through NNPricer.load. Commit the two .pt files (under 1 MB total), or publish them as a release asset with a SHA-256 and a download step in CI, so the 18 skipped tests actually run. Store the training metadata (data hash, box, seed, torch version, benchmark output) in the checkpoint, and generate the README numbers from it. Make NNPricer.load default to retrain_if_missing=False: an 8+ minute data generation plus training run is a surprising side effect for a 'load' call.

findings.title: NN benchmark: the MAE excludes 39% of options (the whole OTM-call wing), filters on the NN's own output, is scored at the training centre only; the speedup is inflated by the non-converging solver
findings.description: The benchmark computes MAE only where heston_ivs>=0.02 & nn_ivs>=0.02. Every OTM call where the reference solver failed returns 1e-4, so the whole x>0.077 wing (194 of 500 options, prices up to $48) is excluded. Filtering on nn_ivs, the prediction under evaluation, is data snooping. Those excluded strikes are exactly where the training set is missing most of its labels (see nngreeks-nn-training-domain). The benchmark also uses the single parameter set at the centre of the +/-30% training box and a single T=0.25, so it measures interpolation at the densest point of the training distribution. Speed: because some entries never converge, the Heston leg's IV inversion always runs the full 50 Newton iterations. In the measurement below, that inversion is 57% of the Heston-leg time. A converging solver cuts it roughly tenfold, so the published 8.1x ratio is inflated by about 2x by the bug. The '8.1x' is also a single machine-dependent sample that is not stored anywhere reproducible.
findings.evidence: Benchmark inputs (seed 42, baseline params, T=0.25): 194/500 options excluded, x range [0.077, 0.254]. Reference IVs for excluded options: x=0.091 $48.11 gives 0.1773; x=0.117 $16.26 gives 0.1572; x=0.154 $1.32 gives 0.1292. Timing, best of 15: heston_call_batch 12.4 ms; shipped IV inversion 16.7 ms on 500 options (50 iterations) vs 1.6 ms on the 306 converging rows. Manaster-Koehler start: 16 iterations, 500/500 valid. A reduced retrain of the shipped code (150k rows, 25 epochs, val MAE 0.168 vp) at the training centre, T=0.25, scored against a quad reference on options priced >$0.01: benchmark-style subset x<=0.077 MAE 0.172 vp; excluded wing x>0.077 MAE 2.359 vp (14x worse); all options 0.963 vp.
findings.proposed_fix: Benchmark against a converged reference: the fixed solver plus a quad-based Heston price for the wing, with a price floor. Report MAE and 99th-percentile error over all well-posed options, never filter on NN output, and break results down by moneyness bucket. Evaluate on a held-out test set of parameter sets drawn from the full calibration domain (see nngreeks-nn-training-domain) and on several maturities, including the archived joint_cal_*.pkl params. Time both legs with the fixed solver, over several slices (full-surface calibration workloads). Record machine, threads and torch version, and publish the median and IQR of the speedup. Update README:153 and substack:18 with the regenerated numbers.

findings.title: NN surrogate trained on a +/-30% box around one day's fit: 0/33 archived calibrations fall inside it; OTM-call labels are 51-77% missing; no domain guard; NN used nowhere in production
findings.description: Parameters are sampled from U[0.7p0, 1.3p0] around baseline_2026-03-24: kappa [3.24,6.01], theta [0.054,0.099], sigma [0.59,1.09], rho [-0.95,-0.665], v0 [0.039,0.073]. The live calibrations all sit elsewhere: v0 is 1e-4..0.022 in every live fit, and kappa runs 1.7..12.9. The surrogate would therefore extrapolate on every real use, and inference has no domain check. Horvath, Muguruza and Tomas (2021) sample uniformly over the admissible parameter domain (e.g. rho in U[-0.95,-0.1]) and keep a separate test set (68k train / 12k test). Here there is neither. Validation data drives early stopping and the LR schedule and is then reported as the model's accuracy. Because failed inversions are dropped, the training labels are biased away from the OTM-call wing. The module docstring says the networks 'replace expensive Heston pricing in the hot calibration loop' and save 'hours vs minutes' in backtesting, but no production code imports nn_pricer except for risk_monitor's use of the IV helper. The tests query rho=-0.99, which is outside the retrained box.
findings.evidence: Every file in data_store/calibrations/joint_cal_*.pkl lies outside the sampled box (0/33, including the 2026-03-24 fit itself, which has rho=-0.99). For example, 2026-09-11 (kappa 5.00, theta 0.0431, v0 0.0109) and 2026-08-21 (kappa 12.86, theta 0.0278, v0 1e-4). Label coverage of the regenerated training parquet against the expected ~45,454 rows per x-bucket: [0.10,0.15) 73%, [0.15,0.20) 49%, [0.20,0.25) 23%. Kept labels are accurate (median 0.000 vp vs quad reference). Reduced retrain evaluated at T=0.25 with a quad reference: 2026-09-11 params MAE 2.24 vp (wing 7.10 vp); 2026-07-01 3.31 vp (wing 7.18); 2026-08-21 9.28 vp (wing 22.29, max 23.3), vs 0.96 vp at the training centre. grep for nn_pricer/NNPricer/HestonNet outside the module and its tests finds only risk_monitor.py:80 (the IV helper).
findings.proposed_fix: Sample over the calibration bounds, or over a realistic superset of the archived fits: log-uniform kappa in [0.1,20], theta in [1e-3,0.5], v0 in [1e-4,0.5], sigma in [0.05,2], rho in U[-0.95,0]. Oversample the regions where fits actually land. Split by parameter set into train/val/test and report test metrics. Store the box in the checkpoint and raise, or warn and fall back to heston_call_batch, when inputs are outside it. Either wire the NN into JointCalibrator behind a flag, with an end-to-end check that NN-calibrated params reproduce the FFT fit within X vp, or re-label C5 in README/docstring as a research prototype that is not used in production. Test: a held-out test-set MAE assertion plus an out-of-domain guard test.

findings.title: 'Unstable node' detection is a pooled, scale-invariant cross-sectional z-score: it always flags about 3 long-dated wing nodes whatever the market regime
findings.description: is_unstable = |vomma - mean(vomma)| > 2 std, pooled over every maturity and strike of one surface. (1) The measure is relative, so scaling all vomma by any constant leaves the flags unchanged: it cannot tell a calm book from a stressed one. (2) Raw vomma is roughly proportional to S*sqrt(T)*phi(d1)*d1*d2/sigma, so pooling across maturities just picks the longest-dated wings. Raw vomma is also larger when IV is low, so the metric is inverted relative to stress. (3) Relative to vega, the most vol-convex nodes are short-dated OTM (top vomma/vega: 30d x=+0.093), and the z-score ranks them lowest. The docstring rationale ('Standard delta-hedging is insufficient ... at these nodes') is a non-sequitur: delta hedging never neutralises vega or vomma at any node.
findings.evidence: Scaling vomma 10x gives identical flags (checked programmatically: True). Across regimes with the corrected solver: calm (v0=0.01, sigma=0.3) flags 4 nodes at [180,365]d with max vomma 21,929; stress (v0=0.36, sigma=1.5) flags 4 at [180,365]d with max vomma 7,131; live 2026-09-11 params flag 3 at [180,365]d. Calm raw vomma exceeds stress raw vomma by 3x. The corrected rho=-0.99 surface's top-3 by vomma/vega are (30d,+0.093) 66.2, (180d,+0.211) 44.1, (91d,+0.132) 31.9.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace it with an absolute, interpretable risk measure, for example the scenario P&L per unit of vega for a vol-of-vol shock sized from VVIX: 0.5*vomma*dsigma^2 / (vega*dsigma), which reduces to 0.5*d1*d2*dsigma/sigma. Alternatively z-score each node against its own history, or within maturity. Document the thresholds and units. Keep the old z-score only as a descriptive rank. Test: flags must scale with a vol-of-vol shock (0 flags when dsigma=0), and must differ between calm and stressed params.

findings.title: Greeks heatmap: 0.05-wide bins collide on the 0.0393-spaced grid, and iloc[0] silently hides 16 of 69 nodes, including 1 of the 3 unstable nodes; QV 'mean' and 'max' bars are identical
findings.description: The strike grid is linspace(-0.30,0.25,15), spacing 0.0393. floor(x/0.05)*0.05 maps pairs of nodes into the -0.30, -0.15, +0.05 and +0.20 bins, and only cell_df.iloc[0] is drawn. Floating-point floor also puts x=0.25 into the +0.20 column. The unstable node at 365d x=-0.2607 (z=+2.05) is hidden behind x=-0.30, although it is listed in the banner and table. qv_convexity is one value per maturity, so the 'Mean QV' and 'Max QV' series plot the same numbers twice. vega_labels/vega_values are computed but never rendered.
findings.evidence: Ran load_page3() in a private copy: n_cells 69, heatmap cells shown 53, unstable shown in heatmap 2 vs n_unstable 3. Columns: ['-0.30','-0.25','-0.20','-0.15','-0.10','-0.05','+0.00','+0.05','+0.10','+0.15','+0.20']. qv_mean == qv_max == [0.0068, 0.0592, 0.3696, 1.0296, 4.6242, 15.9343]. grep -c 'vega_values' greeks.html returns 0.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the actual grid points as columns (round log_moneyness to 4 dp, or index by strike number), since every maturity shares the same x grid by construction. If binning is kept, assert at most one node per (T, bin). Plot a single QV series (the per-maturity value) or the exact closed form. Remove or render the vega series. Test: in load_page3, the count of non-null heatmap cells equals n_cells, and the count of unstable cells equals n_unstable.

findings.title: Greeks page: hard-coded or false captions, wrong axis definition, unitless Greeks, and a failure mode that renders a green '0 / 0' all-clear
findings.description: Hard-coded: '6 maturities', the date '2026-03-24', 'Across all 69 nodes', 'All three unstable nodes are at the 1-year maturity', 'Max: 365d maturity nodes' and 'Min: Near-expiry nodes'. The last is false: the minimum vomma of -119 is at 365d x=+0.014 (1Y ATM). The axis is labelled ln(K/S), but the data is ln(K/F). The legend says 'Low vomma'/'High vomma', but the colour encodes the z-score, and 'Unstable (z > 2)' should read |z|>2. The vanna caption attributes negative mean BS vanna to 'the leverage effect'. BS vanna is a sensitivity that does not depend on rho, and the negative mean comes from an ITM-heavy grid with the OTM wing dropped; it turns positive at 180d/365d once fixed. Averaging vanna across strikes without position weights has no risk meaning. The QV caption ('sensitivity of the straddle P&L to variance path roughness ... reflects accumulated vomma exposure') is wrong: the quantity is Var[integral of v dt], a model quantity independent of any option's vomma. The scatter caption blames 'vol-of-vol accumulation', but vomma's sqrt(T) growth is plain BS. No units appear anywhere. vomma is $ per (1.00 vol)^2 per unit of index, so 4,086 means $0.41 per vol-pt^2, or $40.9 per SPX contract. If the parquet fails to load, greeks_error is never rendered, and the page returns HTTP 200 with a green '0 / 0' Unstable Nodes card. freeze_site only checks for 'Traceback', so that page would deploy.
findings.evidence: Rendered /greeks via the Flask test client with the parquet moved away (private copy): status 200, card 'green 0 / 0', badge '0 nodes . 6 maturities . 2026-03-24', no error text. Live greeks.html contains every hard-coded string listed above. The parquet row with minimum vomma is T_days=365, log_moneyness=0.0143, vomma=-119.06.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive every count, date and location claim from the data (n_maturities, as_of_date, where the max/min actually sit, T_days of the unstable nodes). Change the axis label to ln(K/F). Relabel the legend as z-score colours and |z|>2. Quote Greeks in desk units (vega per vol pt = /100, vomma per vol-pt^2 = /1e4, optionally x100 multiplier) with explicit unit labels. Rewrite the vanna, QV and scatter captions correctly, or drop the mean-vanna chart. Render greeks_error as a red banner, give the card a neutral state when n_cells==0, and make freeze_site fail when a page carries an error marker. Test: rendering with a missing parquet shows the error banner and no green card; the badge date equals the parquet as_of_date.

findings.title: C7 vomma 'unstable day' flag can never fire: it z-scores a single-call vomma at 2020 spot against a 2026 surface (0/253 days flagged, including the COVID crash)
findings.description: The straddle's vomma is computed as one call's vomma, but a straddle's vomma is 2x the call's (put vomma equals call vomma). It is then z-scored against the mean and std of the C6 surface built at S=6,581 across all maturities and strikes. Vomma is linear in S, so a 2020 book at S of about 3,257 sits at z<0 almost every day, and the flag is structurally dead. report_generator nevertheless states 'P&L residuals are elevated on days matching these conditions', which no day ever matches. It separately discloses the S mismatch in its table.
findings.evidence: data_store/backtest/delta_hedge_2020.parquet: vomma_zscore max 0.157, mean -0.817; is_unstable.sum() = 0 of 253. On 2020-03-16 (VIX about 82), z = -0.673.
findings.proposed_fix: Use straddle vomma (2*call vomma). Normalise by S or by vega (d1*d2/sigma). Z-score against the position's own rolling history, or use an absolute threshold in P&L terms (see nngreeks-unstable-node-metric). Remove the unsupported sentence from report_generator. Test: a synthetic path with a vol-of-vol spike must produce at least one flag.

findings.title: train_network's passed_target accepts an SPX MAE up to 10 vol pts (100x the 0.1 vp target); VIX metrics are labelled 'vol pts'; the VIX val split leaks parameter sets
findings.description: mae_vol_pts = MAE*100 is already in vol points for the SPX network, yet passed_target tests mae_vol_pts < 10.0. The comment '<0.1 vol pt in decimal = 10 in percent' confuses the units; config says NN_VOL_ERROR_TARGET = 0.001 (0.1 vp). For NN-2 the same number is VIX points x100 but is printed as 'vol pts'. 'Train MAE (raw)' prints the validation MAE again. train_vix row-shuffles the 500k set (df.sample) before the positional 90/10 split, so each parameter set's 10 tenors land on both sides, and the reported val MAE is not out-of-sample. The SPX split, by contrast, is by contiguous parameter-set blocks.
findings.evidence: Tiny shim run: passed_target=True with mae_vol_pts=0.794 and 0.524. Reduced retrain: passed_target=True with val MAE 0.168 vp (>0.1 target). VIX split on the regenerated data: 82.6% of val rows share their exact (kappa,theta,sigma,v0) with training rows. SPX: 1 of 501 val parameter sets is shared (the boundary set).
findings.proposed_fix: Compare against config.NN_VOL_ERROR_TARGET*100 for SPX and a separate VIX-points target for NN-2. Report metrics in each model's native units, with labels. Split by parameter-set id (GroupShuffleSplit) and add a held-out test split. Test: assert passed_target is False for a model with 0.5 vp MAE.

findings.title: NN-2 (VIX) 'acceleration' is about 5-10x slower than the closed-form expression it approximates
findings.description: The NN-2 target heston_vix_futures_curve is the closed form sqrt(theta + (E[v_T]-theta)(1-e^{-kappa*tau})/(kappa*tau)). A 4x64 MLP adds approximation error and costs more than evaluating that formula directly.
findings.evidence: Best of 200, 8 tenors, single thread: closed-form loop 12.5 us, vectorised closed form 7.1 us, NN-2 forward 68.2 us.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete NN-2 and call the closed form (vectorise heston_vix_futures_curve). If a VIX surrogate is wanted, target something without a closed form, such as VIX options or futures with the Jensen/convexity term. Update README/docstrings accordingly.

findings.title: Vomma and 'volga' are the same Greek, but the code, dashboard, README and substack present them as distinct; the docstring promises a cross-check that does not exist
findings.description: The 'volga' column is a central finite-difference estimate of the analytic 'vomma' (d2V/dsigma2). It is a numerical self-check, not a second Greek. The subtitle 'Vomma . Volga . Vanna', the README's 'Vomma/vanna/volga surface' and the substack's 'vomma, vanna, volga' imply three risk measures. The module header also advertises a forward-difference vega check, (Vega(sigma+d)-Vega(sigma))/d, which is not implemented, and the test docstring's '20 tests across 6 classes' is stale (42 tests, 8 classes).
findings.evidence: Parquet: max |volga-vomma| / |vomma| is about 6e-4. Both columns are the same quantity. Dashboard never displays 'volga'.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the column vomma_fd_check (or keep it out of the published parquet). Say 'vomma (a.k.a. volga)' once in the UI and docs, fix the header docstring, and list vanna, vomma and QV variance as the published measures.

findings.title: QV convexity is estimated by noisy Monte Carlo although an exact CIR closed form exists; the scheme is mislabelled
findings.description: Var[integral_0^T v dt] under CIR has an exact expression: 2*integral_0^T Var(v_s)(1-e^{-kappa(T-s)})/kappa ds, where Var(v_s) = v0*sigma^2/kappa*(e^{-kappa s}-e^{-2 kappa s}) + theta*sigma^2/(2 kappa)*(1-e^{-kappa s})^2. The MC version uses 10k paths and 100 steps with a right-endpoint Riemann sum. The docstring calls the scheme Lord et al. (2010) 'full truncation', but because it truncates the state after every step it is the 'absorption' variant.
findings.evidence: Published values vs exact: 14d +1.8%, 30d +2.9%, 60d +0.7%, 91d 0.0%, 180d +0.8%, 365d +0.6%. A 200k-path, 2,000-step run is within -0.2..-0.3% of exact.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the closed form, via one quad or its analytic integral, which is exact, deterministic and microseconds. Keep the MC only as a unit-test cross-check, with a corrected scheme name, the trapezoid rule and full truncation.

findings.title: In-scope tests tolerate or vacuously pass the defects above; no test compares surface IVs to an independent reference
findings.description: test_roundtrip_skew_range allows 5% of IVs to be wrong by more than 0.01 and checks for NaNs that the solver never produces. test_row_count accepts up to 4 of 10 nodes dropped. test_vomma_full_surface_far_otm_positive only guards `if len(far_otm) > 0`. In the fast grid its single far-OTM row has a garbage IV (30d K=7400: 0.0458 vs a reference of about 0.09), and the 30d K=7000 node is silently dropped. validate()'s vomma_positive_far_otm is vacuous on the call side because those nodes are dropped. A test applying the corrected solver still passes the whole in-scope suite: 124 passed, 24 skipped, so no test detects the bug.
findings.evidence: test_roundtrip_skew_range sample: NaN 0, err>0.01: 3 (x=0.169 T=0.743 true 0.133 returns 1e-4). The _make_surface() rows show 8 of 10 nodes and iv 0.0458 at 30d x=+0.115. The mutated copy (Manaster-Koehler start plus NaN on non-convergence) ran test_risk_monitor, test_nn_pricer and test_delta_hedger: 124 passed, 24 skipped.
findings.proposed_fix: Tighten the round-trip test (0 failures, max err <1e-8 on a dense grid). Add a reference test against quad+brentq Heston IVs for the default surface. Make the far-OTM tests assert that nodes are present. Add load_page3 tests (heatmap cell count, units, error banner).

findings.title: The Greeks monitor, delta hedger and backtest engine import torch and sklearn only to reach a private IV helper; torch.load(weights_only=False)
findings.description: risk_monitor imports _bs_iv_vectorized from nn_pricer, so importing the backtest engine loads torch and sklearn. A private NN-module function has become shared infrastructure. The checkpoints hold only tensors, lists, strings and numbers, yet they are loaded with weights_only=False, which permits arbitrary pickle execution.
findings.evidence: python -X importtime -c 'import joint_vol_calibration.backtest.backtest_engine': nn_pricer cumulative 1.73 s of 3.19 s; 'torch' in sys.modules is True, as is sklearn.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the (fixed) vectorised IV solver into models/black_scholes.py, or next to implied_vol_from_price in heston.py, and import it from both nn_pricer and risk_monitor. Use torch.load(..., weights_only=True).

checked_ok: Checked the analytic BS Greeks with dividend yield in risk_monitor (_bs_call_price, _bs_delta, _bs_vega, _bs_vomma, _bs_vanna) against mpmath 40-digit derivatives on 300 random (S,K,T,r,q,sigma) cases: all agree to 7.6e-14 relative or better. vanna=-e^{-qT} phi(d1) d2/sigma and vomma=vega*d1*d2/sigma are correct.

Checked the volga central difference (bump 1e-3). It matches analytic vomma to about 6e-4 relative on the published parquet, with a worst case of 0.76% on extreme random inputs. Bump size and roundoff are fine.

Checked the ITM-side (x<0) IVs from heston_call_batch plus the shipped solver. They agree with an independent Lewis/Carr-Madan quad plus brentq reference to about 1e-4. The failures are confined to the OTM-call wing.

Reproduced the published greeks_surface.parquet exactly (max |iv| diff 3.3e-13) with kappa=4.62, theta=0.0764, sigma=0.84, rho=-0.99, v0=0.0561, S=6581, r=0.045, q=0.013. Its provenance is now established.
QV convexity MC is within 0-2.9% of the exact CIR closed form. Its values are directionally correct.
SPX NN train/val split holds out by parameter set: only 1 of 501 validation parameter sets is shared with training. The StandardScaler is fit on training rows only and stored in the checkpoint.
NN SPX training labels come from the semi-analytic CF pricer, not MC. Where kept, they match the quad reference (median 0.000 vp, p95 0.000 vp).
HestonNet architecture, SiLU activations and Softplus output are as documented. The parameter-count test is correct.
The benchmark's warm-up plus best-of-5 perf_counter timing from the C21 fix is sound steady-state practice. Its remaining problems are what is timed and scored (see findings), not the timer.
The load_page3 unstable-node list is built before binning (FIX 3), so all 3 nodes appear in the banner and table. Only the heatmap hides one.
No look-ahead issues in the in-scope code: the Greeks surface and NN use no time-series data.
The shared repo /home/user/vol-system-dashboard was not modified. All runs used private copies under scratchpad/audit/nngreeks and nngreeks_fix.
